item.title: Cavaliers' Mario Hezonja shines on Croatian Heritage Night vs. Pacers
item.description: CLEVELAND — A glimpse of Europe was in the stands Nov. 20 for Croatian Heritage Night as the Cavaliers took on the Indiana Pacers . "It means so much for us to get this opportunity for our Croatian community, to come together," a Croatian fan told the Beacon Journal. Nearly 400 Croatian fans sat pregame to watch Cavs forward Mario Hezonja and Pacers center Ivica Zubac, who are Croatia natives. Hezonja was able to talk to fans before he warmed up, then thanked them for coming out and sat with them for a group photo. "It means a lot if they're happy," Hezonja said after collecting 10 points and 10 rebounds in 20 minutes of the bench to help the Cavs beat the Pacers 128-119 on a night James Harden poured in 51 points. "They have somebody that is fighting for them on a court, that type of stuff. We are from a very small country, so it's super, super proud that I have that much support from the community like this." Cleveland is still fairly new for Hezonja, so being able to have a taste of home before a game meant a lot to him. “First of all, big congratulations and big thank you to my team, organization, the whole organization to getting this done," he said. "It's not easy having a brand-new player that just got back after six years, who’s Croatian, and then to organize something like this is huge. "I was also shocked by the number of how many people showed up. I know for sure some of the people couldn't make it, which I'm sad about it, so I want everybody to be together for these types of night, to be here.” Many fans felt the appreciation, too. They were given scarves and were wearing jerseys from their national soccer team. Some were even dressed in traditional clothing from Croatia. "Both my parents are straight off the boat — they came in the late '60s — we're here, first generation do a little bit of both old and new country," another fan said. "I'm trying to make sure [daughter] Emma is a part of that because it's very important for her to embrace the culture." Mario Hezonja's impact on the Cavaliers Hezonja was a lottery pick in the 2015 NBA draft, selected No. 5 overall by the Orlando Magic. After bouncing around the league, he left the NBA after six years to return to Europe, playing in Greece, Russia and Spain. The one-year, $2.8 million contract Hezonja signed over the summer became fully guaranteed on Nov. 15. Cavs general manager Koby Altman and coach Kenny Atkinson saw what Hezonja brings to the team and his impact early on. "Thank you, Koby, thank you organization and thanks to my teammates," Hezonja said. "They've been the ones that trust me. Thanks, Kenny and the coaching staff. They've been huge, huge help with me. My NBA career is in their hands. "I'm trying to help the best way I can. Today was the double-double. The next day is going to be something else. I'm an open book, open-minded about everything, so keep doing it.” With his playing time increasing, Hezonja has upped his averages to 9.1 points, 5.4 rebounds and 1.8 assists

item.title: Jordan Stolz nears becoming youngest speed skater to reach 50 World Cup wins
item.description: Jordan Stolz, after an offseason of change , opened the post-Olympic season with podium finishes in his first three races, including his 48th career World Cup win. Stolz, a 22-year-old who won two golds and one silver at the Milan Cortina Olympics, claimed the 500m in a track record in Obihiro, Japan, on Saturday. About 90 minutes later, he took second in the 1500m, 21 hundredths behind Ning Zhongyan of China, who also relegated Stolz to runner-up in that event at the Milan Cortina Olympics. Earlier on Friday, Stolz was third in the 1000m in Obihiro, snapping a 14-race World Cup win streak at that distance dating to 2023 (counting A division races only). The last time Stolz was beaten in a World Cup 1000m was Nov. 10, 2023, when he finished third in that season's opener in Obihiro. He owns the 1000m world record of 1:05.37 set in Kearns, Utah, on Jan. 26, 2024. Stolz is slated to race another 500m in Obihiro on the last day of the stop on Sunday, live on Peacock . Stolz is two wins from becoming the youngest speed skater — by nearly five years — to reach 50 individual World Cup victories, according to Speedskatingstats.com. Jeremy Wotherspoon of Canada, a sprint star in the 1990s and 2000s, is currently the youngest to do so — at age 27. Stolz would be one of the youngest athletes across all winter sports to reach that milestone. Younger than Alpine skier Mikaela Shiffrin (who was 23 years old in 2018) and Norwegian cross-country skier Johannes Høsflot Klæbo (who was 26 in 2022). Japanese ski jumper Sara Takanashi did it younger at age 20 in 2017. The only male speed skaters with more individual World Cup wins are Wotherspoon (67) and American Shani Davis (58), who advises Stolz. The overall record holder in speed skating is German Gunda Niemann, who won 98 times. After Obihiro, Stolz can target 50 at the next World Cup in Heerenveen, Netherlands, from Dec. 4-6. Heerenveen's famed Thialf arena will host speed skating at the 2030 Alps Winter Olympics. item.title: James Harden boosts Cavaliers with memorable 51-point game vs. Pacers
item.description: CLEVELAND — Cavaliers point guard James Harden dribbled with his left hand as he drove to the basket against Indiana guard Quenton Jackson, maneuvered between Jackson and Pacers center Jay Huff and then used his right hand to make a layup as time expired in the third quarter. The left-handed shooting Harden was immediately greeted by Cavaliers teammates who were in awe of the move and his scoring outburst. Wing Peyton Watson yelled in Harden's face with unbridled enthusiasm, and guard Donovan Mitchell placed both of his hands atop his head as if his mind had been blown. "I think that's the joy that we have to bring for each other on a night-to-night basis, even when things aren't going well," Harden said. "The excitement that we have for each other is contagious." The Cavs reveled in a memorable night for Harden, who scored a game-high 51 points in their 128-119 victory over the Indiana Pacers on Friday, Nov. 20, at Rocket Arena. By triumphing in an NBA Cup Game, the Cavs (9-8) improved to 2-1 in East Group B. The 37-year-old Harden played as if he had borrowed the Cup during pregame warm-ups, dipped it in the fountain of youth and chugged. "Vintage performance — very reminiscent of his Houston days," Cavs coach Kenny Atkinson said of Harden, who won the 2017-18 NBA Most Valuable Player award with the Rockets. Harden passed the late Kobe Bryant for the third-most 50-point games in NBA history with 26. Only Wilt Chamberlain (118) and Michael Jordan (31) have more. "Obviously, Wilt was elite, but you've got Mike and Kobe, [at the] shooting guard position, they were just the best to ever do it," Harden said. "So, just to be in that conversation, it's very humbling, and it's definitely special." Harden said he thought he could have a prolific scoring night "from the jump." He wound up with his highest point total since the Cavs acquired him this past February in a trade that sent point guard Darius Garland to the Los Angeles Clippers. Harden scored 15 points in the first quarter, nine in the second, 18 in the third and nine in the fourth, when he accounted for seven of Cleveland's final nine points to ensure a rally by Indiana (5-11) would fall short. While Harden fielded the question in the Cavs locker room, Mitchell walked behind the scrum of reporters surrounding his teammate and chimed in by saying "y'all did" doubt Harden could do it. Later, Mitchell said, "I'm glad he had a night like this tonight because I felt like a lot of people were getting on him a little bit. And I think that's one way to answer it. Do we expect it every night? No, but if he does it, great. But I think the biggest thing is to see him in that form — aggressive. You're looking at one of the greatest players of all time. It's definitely good to see, amazing to see." Atkinson said Harden is "just getting into form, getting into better shape" lately. Atkinson explained Harden's contractual situation this past summer kept him from sticking to his typical offseason routine filled with pickup basketball. He re-signed with the Cavs for three years and $97 million, yet the two sides waited for other moves to materialize first and didn't agree to the deal until Aug. 20. The delay gave the team financial flexibility, aiding its sign-and-trade move for Watson. "After that, I started to ramp up, ramp up, ramp up," Harden said. item.description: What happened when Juventus last beat Venezia? The Men’s First Team are back in Serie A action after the international break, this time taking on Venezia at the Allianz Stadium in the 12:30 CET slot on Sunday, November 22. The Bianconeri are currently pushing to get into the European places, whilst Venezia sit in the relegation zone and will be hoping to cause an upset. Let’s take a look at the last time Juventus beat Venezia. Champions League football secured Venezia have bounced between Serie A and Serie B frequently in recent years, meaning the last clash between the Arancioneroverdi and the Bianconeri came in May 2025. It proved to be an incredibly important one for both teams, with Juventus clinching a Champions League place and Venezia being relegated. The match at the Stadio Pier Luigi Penzo began in dramatic fashion, with Daniel Fila putting Venezia ahead after just two minutes. It seemed that just two minutes later, Juventus had equalised, but Alberto Costa’s excellent strike was ruled out for a handball. It took another 20 minutes before the equaliser did come. Kenan Yildiz charged at the Venezia defence and they gave him enough space to get a shot on target, which went underneath Andrei Radu. In a flash, Juventus had turned the game around. The ball broke on the edge of the box for Randal Kolo Muani, who charged into the box and fired past Radu, making it 2-1 to the Bianconeri. Despite falling behind, Eusebio Di Francesco’s side rallied in the second half and soon found an equaliser, with Ridgeciano Haps scoring and making it 2-2. Just after Michele Di Gregorio produced a fine save to keep the score level, Francisco Conceicao won a penalty thanks to his quick feet. Manuel Locatelli stepped up and scored, putting Juventus back in control. There were contrasting scenes at full-time, as Igor Tudor’s side celebrated Champions League qualification, and Venezia’s players and fans came to terms with relegation. View this post on YouTube

item.title: Kane vows to be back for ‘business end of the season’ after surgery
item.description: Bayern Munich's Harry Kane (L) receives treatment for an injury during the German Bundesliga soccer match between Bayern Munich and Cologne at Allianz Arena. (is associated with: «Kane vows to be back for ‘business end of the season’ after surgery») Tom Weller/dpa Harry Kane is targeting the “business end of the season” after undergoing surgery on a torn ligament in his left ankle. Bayern Munich said the operation on the injury, sustained in Friday’s 1-1 draw with Cologne, was a success but the 33-year-old is expected to be out for months as a result. Kane wrote on Instagram: “The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it’s an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. “I’ll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season! “Tough times don’t last, tough people do” – my guy @edelman11 (Julian Edelman, three-time Super Bowl winner with the New England Patriots) told me this one! “Thank you for all the messages! Alles gut.” The end of the message is German for "Everything’s fine." Kane sustained the injury when he was scythed down in the area by Cologne defender Joel Schmied, who reached Michael Olise’s low cross first but clattered into the Ballon d’Or winner’s left leg in his follow-through at the back post. The England captain writhed in pain and, although he gingerly got back to his feet and initially soldiered on, it was clear he could not continue and he hobbled off the field alongside two physios after treatment. After the match Bayern confirmed Kane had torn the syndesmotic ligament and “will therefore be sidelined for the next few months”. Kane earlier this month signed a new deal with the Bundesliga giants until June 2029 – reportedly worth in excess of £400,000 ($517,600) a week, making him the highest-paid player in Europe before bonuses. Since arriving from Tottenham three years ago, Kane has bagged a scarcely believable 156 goals in 163 appearances in all competitions, helping Bayern win a league and cup double last season. He went into the international break having a drawn a blank in his four previous matches for Bayern but he scored twice for England, including from the spot in their 3-2 Nations League win over Spain. But after being forced off after 20 minutes at the Allianz Arena, replaced by Tom Bischof, Kane could now be facing a battle to be fully fit for England’s two-legged quarter-final against Norway in March.

item.description: Hutch, we needed you on the field I grew up watching the Lions on black and white TV in the days of Milt Plum, Lem Barney, Joe Schmidt, Dick "Night Train" Lane and Tommy Watkins. I have been a Detroit Lions fan since the early 1960s, and I have seen the NFL change for the good and for the not so good. The thing that bothers me greatly is how today's players make everything about them, not the team. In this modern era of the NFL, there is one player who was the consummate pro in how he conducted himself on the field of play, and that was Barry Sanders. After one of his spectacular runs or touchdowns, he didn't run and chest bump a teammate, he didn't spike the ball, he didn't run and jump into the stands, he just handed the ball to the referee. I'm saying all of this to address Aidan Hutchinson's injury, that was avoidable! He wasn't hurt on a play, he was hurt celebrating a sack, something he gets paid to do, something he is supposed to do. Because of his actions, he is lost for the season as the Lions make a playoff run, and his season is over. More importantly, he has let his team down. As a star player at his position, he needs to understand his importance to the team and act accordingly. Today's players make what they do about them, look at me, see what I did. Just do your job and let that speak for itself, like Barry did. High five a teammate, don't put more stress on your body than the game already does. I recall some years ago another Lion did the same thing and was lost for the season due to injury. Hutch, we need you on the field, not on crutches. Gennaro Gattuso took over in the dugout at a time when his managerial stock was undeniably low after failing to qualify for the World Cup with Italy. The squad he inherited finished ninth last term and saw many key players depart over the summer. Some shrewd reinforcements did come, most notably midfielder Davide Frattesi who scored in each of his first three games with the club, but not to a degree which should have precipitated this early success. And yet, Gattuso has made this side more than the sum of its parts, as Frattesi is one of three players with four goals to lead an attack that has seen 12 different goalscorers. The staunchest back line in the league thus far has been anchored by Oliver Provstgaard, who few would have predicted to show such consistency after serving largely as a reserve last year. He’s been partnered by both Josip Sutalo, on loan from Ajax, and Danilho Doekhi, who joined on a free transfer from Union Berlin. A pair of Lotito-esque, low-budget signings that didn’t turn heads when they joined but have exceeded expectations. Nuno Tavares is back close to his best at left back and the right flank has been dutifully manned by Romano Floriani Mussolini, the much-talked about great-grandson of Benito Mussolini who has let his stellar play do the talking. Gustav Isaksen and Tijjani Noslin join Frattesi as the joint top goal scorers, while Mattia Zaccagni has provided his usual consistency and leadership to round out the attack. Reda Belahayne has flourished as the team’s regista , finally coming good after a January 2025 move from Hellas Verona. He’s filling in for the still-injured Nicolò Rovella, whose return will only bolster what’s been a formidable midfield to this point. Speaking of which, Kenneth Taylor has now fully settled after joining this past winter from Ajax and ties the side together between the lines. Gattuso’s approach received a bit of a refresh, too, as Lazio play intricate attacking football and mainly keep the ball on the ground as they progress fluidly up the pitch. Patterns of play are evident and a positional understanding between players has produced some fun-to-watch attacking moves. They’ve constructed the 5th-most attacks of 10-or-more passes in Serie A (166) and average the fourth-most passes per build-up sequence (4.23). Patience has been a virtue for the Biancocelesti , also ranking sixth in the league in average possession (53.7%). The staunch defense isn’t the result of a smothering press either, with Lazio preferring solidity and organization as they are near the bottom of Serie A in pressed sequences (99, 16th) and seventh in passes per defensive action (12.7). This means that they do employ pressure, but it’s calculated and not constant. It’s also helped that Christos Mandas is having a career year between the posts, keeping four clean sheets while his 5.88 goals prevented are second in the division. Despite all of the reasons for praise, there are still some concerns when it comes to the underlying numbers. Gattuso’s men have overperformed their expected goals by a whopping 7.66, and opponents have scored 4.62 less goals than expected. This suggests that the truth lies somewhere in between their league-leading actual figures and fairly pedestrian xG marks. Nonetheless, the Biancocelesti ’s next three fixtures after the international break are favorable on paper: at home to Lecce, away against Torino and back home versus a struggling Atalanta side. After that comes the derby against Roma, with their rivals also in the early title race, making for one of the highest-stakes clashes between the capital clubs in years. There’s a lot of season left and plenty of time for Lazio to stumble from their early pedestal. There are indications that this should happen, but they’ve already defied a lot of odds to be on top at this stage in the first place. The same can be said of the fans, who’ve proven their determination in defying Lotito long ago. Then the real question becomes, what will give first? A slide down the table or Lazio’s fans returning as they truly lock horns in a scudetto challenge come March? One of the most intriguing storylines in European football has plenty left to unfold as clubs resume this weekend. Stay tuned.

item.title: Bayern Munich considering Jamal Musiala sale after health problems
item.description: Bayern Munich are considering selling Jamal Musiala over concerns that his ongoing health problems will prevent him from returning to his best form. Musiala, 23, was diagnosed with a “neurological dysfunction” after suffering an on-pitch collapse twice in a matter of days during pre-season friendlies against Heidenheim and RB Leipzig. The Germany international said he was “very optimistic... there is no additional health risk beyond this” and indicated the condition would not hamper his highly promising career. However, Bayern chief Karl-Heinz Rummenigge has now admitted that the club are assessing his future amid a downturn in performances, publicly questioning whether the club can now justify his lofty salary. Rummenigge told Sky Germany : “He has a health-related issue. It's also well known that he has a contract involving very substantial sums of money. As a club, we have to consider how to deal with that situation. I think that's responsible and perfectly normal. “What we know unfortunately suggests it will be difficult for him to get back to the level he has often shown here in this stadium.” Musiala was reportedly Bayern’s best-paid player until Ballon d’Or winner Harry Kane penned a contract extension earlier this month. He has been limited to just four appearances in the Bundesliga this term due to a muscle injury, scoring one goal and notching one assist, with fitness problems continuing to plague him after spending over half of last season out with a broken leg. Rummenigge says “a decision will have to be made” over his Musiala if he fails to show signs of improvement, but admitted that the former Chelsea academy product’s health issues would make a sale difficult. Rummenigge added: “We need to talk to the family, the player, and the agency, because then these sums of money, sorry, with all due respect, are no longer feasible. “I cannot imagine that Jamal wants to leave the club or that any other club would buy him under these conditions. “We are all interested in his return, ideally in top form. But what happens if that isn’t the case? Then we still have to think about the finances. “The discussion hasn’t taken place yet. These are just ideas at this stage.”

item.title: 'I'll be back': vows Kane after ankle surgery
item.description: Bayern Munich striker Harry Kane leaves the pitch with an ankle injury in Friday's Bundesliga match with Cologne. (Karl-Josef HILDENBRAND) Bayern Munich's star striker Harry Kane pledged to return for the "business end of the season" after undergoing surgery on his left ankle on Saturday. Kane limped off after 20 minutes of Bayern's 1-1 home draw with Cologne in their Bundesliga match on Friday, the club confirming the England captain had torn a ligament in his ankle. Bayern issued a statement Saturday saying the Ballon d'Or winner had "successfully undergone surgery" on his left ankle. "The 33-year-old will now begin his rehabilitation program," Bayern said, with the injury expected to keep Kane out for three to four months. Kane posted a picture on social media from his hospital bed on Saturday, vowing to work his way back to fitness this season. "The highs and lows of life! Obviously very disappointed to get this injury but as always it's an opportunity to show resilience and improvement going into 2027. "I'll be back fresh and ready to go for the business end of the season." Kane shared a quote from three-time Super Bowl-winning wide receiver Julian Edelman: "tough times don't last, tough people do", while thanking his supporters for their messages of support. Kane has a history of ankle issues although he has only missed a handful of games since moving to Bayern in 2023. England coach Thomas Tuchel will be keeping a keen eye out on how England's most capped player's rehabilitation progresses. England play Norway in the Nations League quarter-finals in late March. The injury comes at a difficult time for Bayern, who are currently missing several players, particularly up front. Bayern are without Luis Diaz, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies, Ismael Saibari and captain Manuel Neuer, while midfielder Jamal Musiala and coach Vincent Kompany both returned after long lay-offs on Friday. dwi/pi

item.title: Horse Tracks: Does the AFC title go through Denver?
item.description: LAS VEGAS , NV - DECEMBER 7: Nik Bonitto (15) of the Denver Broncos celebrates sacking Geno Smith (7) of the Las Vegas Raiders during the third quarter of the Broncos' 24-17 win at Allegiant Stadium in Las Vegas, Nevada on Sunday, December 7, 2025. (Photo by AAron Ontiveroz/The Denver Post) | Denver Post via Getty Images Good morning, Broncos Country! Several AFC teams swiftly moved up in the conference rankings last weekend while the Broncos quietly dropped to fifth overall, making their path to and through the postseason a little more challenging. But that means nothing to Broncos Country. While the rest of the country was seeing cracks in the Orange and Blue, this fanbase saw more opportunity to flex some muscle in the remaining weeks. And prove some (many) people wrong. While a lot of people believe the road to the Super Bowl will go through the Bills, if not the Bengals, not too many outside of Colorado believe it will go through Denver. Which is kinda awesome, because I’ve always preferred it when Denver plays the role of the underdogs ( versus the overdogs — sorry Bo! ) to the media hype. But man, if Broncos Country just won’t give up on this team! A whopping 64% of fans believe it will be Denver who wins the AFC, which is 46% percent more than the crew picking the Bills (18%) or the number giving the honor to the Bengals (11%). Perhaps my favorite number in the whole survey — even more than the large majority picking the Broncos — is the very small 2% who believe the AFC title will belong to the Chiefs by season’s end. Hahahahahahahahahahahahaha. Either way, nothing happens without winning most if not all of the remaining games, and that starts by taking care of business this weekend at Mile High against the hated Raiduhs .

Despite the hardships endured after spending so long on the sidelines, many did predict that the Spaniard could use this rest time to return reinvigorated at the end of the season . Winning titles in Tokyo, Vienna and Paris has certainly proven that suggestion correct. However, the ATP Finals is the one he will really be keen to capture, and based on his matches so far, it feels hard to bet against him. That being said, it must be noted that Alcaraz has picked up a hamstring injury during his comfortable group-stage run, with Brad Gilbert looking ahead to how this might shape the tournament. Why does Carlos Alcaraz get injured so often? Speaking on the Big T podcast , after he had previewed Carlos Alcaraz ’s upcoming semi-final vs Ben Shelton, the American pundit and coach was asked why he thinks the 23-year-old suffers so often from injury. After all, whilst this year’s wrist issue has been the worst of his career to date, he has endured plenty of health concerns over the years; certainly enough to raise alarm bells. Comparing Alcaraz to Rafael Nadal, whose super-physical play style saw his body break down time and time again, Gilbert insisted: “Well, I mean, injuries are part of every sport. They’re part of tennis. Not everybody can be like Fed and just play elegantly. And actually, Djokovic had an incredibly long run of being pretty healthy as well. “So some players are a little unluckier; some game styles are a little more physical. I do think that Alcaraz’s style is physical, like Rafa. It’s a little bit physically demanding. “Fans want to see the dynamics. They want to see Carlos doing these incredible things out there; sometimes it can be a little bit taxing on the body when you’re running five corners, and then you hit some outrageous shot. I love seeing it myself. But unfortunately, I go back to the, you know, availability is the best availability, and his style, at 23, what do you think it’ll be like when he’s 28? “He’s gonna have some. Same with Rafa, but he managed it for 20 years.” Brad Gilbert previews Carlos Alcaraz’s ATP Finals match vs Ben Shelton Gilbert’s analysis of today’s standout ATP Finals showdown was unsurprisingly dominated by Juan Carlos Ferrero. After all, whilst he did help Shelton during his Paris Masters final defeat to Alcaraz, he was not present in his box. Today, he will be. Gilbert, who actually spoke to Ferrero not long ago, had some advice for the Spanish coach ahead of his first official match against his former pupil. Photo by Dimitar DILKOFF / AFP via Getty Images He suggested: “I think he needs to be a lot more aggressive off the first ball and try to win more points off of the first or second ball, because as the rally kind of gets lengthened, or if Alcaraz gets a ball from neutral, that’s where the pendulum really swings for Carlos. “I think he needs to be a lot more aggressive, and I also like to see him serve way more aggressively. Try to win points off that first serve, you know, ’cause I think that’s more frustrating when you play a big server, and you’re not getting into rallies.” Due to his injury, Alcaraz went big against Flavio Cobolli and reaped the benefits of a quick and easy match. Discussing whether now playing Shelton, who historically likes to keep the points short anyway, will benefit the seven-time major champion, Gilbert added: “I’ve heard you guys talk about, you know, here in Paris, how quick these courts are. And yet I’m seeing a lot of rallies. Actually, Ben does like to get in rallies. “So maybe if you are JCF and Ben and Bryan, you’re thinking about, okay, what you watched today was the guy playing at Mach 10 speed. Maybe we want to try to extend some rallies to see how his movement is. “He had the legs strapped up. He’s got the knees. So he’s a little bit banged up, played a lot of tennis in the last, you know, five, six weeks, after not playing any tennis, and he’s supposedly supposed to play Davis Cup next week.” Gilbert finished by reiterating that, whilst Shelton and Ferrero will want to win this match, his pre-season ahead of the Australian Open is what really matters for their new professional relationship.

Once the Valkyries advanced to the Finals, the concert was moved. A Valkyries representative said it was “standard practice” to have contingency dates for postseason games. Contingency dates are standard practice across NBA arenas. Jerry Goldman, a vice president for booking at the Chicago Bulls’ and Blackhawks’ United Center, told Front Office Sports the United Center ensures that contracts for events such as concerts and private events scheduled from April to June—normally the NBA and NHL playoffs window—include backup dates. “When you book during the playoffs, they know,” Goldman said. “We put it in their agreement like, ‘Your contingency date is this.’ Everybody knows.” The Washington Spirit are going to incorporate contingency dates going forward, the team’s CEO Kim Stone told FOS on Thursday at NWSL media day. The Spirit’s Audi Field is operated by D.C. United, and a spokesperson for the MLS team told FOS that the stadium booked Nov. 14’s Division III Secretaries Cup between the Merchant Marine Academy and Coast Guard Academy in spring of 2025. “Both partners wanted to be at Audi, and we found a way to make it work,” D.C. United’s president of business operations Danita Johnson, told FOS last week. Stone, who managed arenas for the NBA’s Heat and Warriors before joining the Spirit, credited Johnson for making the NWSL semifinal and Secretaries Cup double-header at Audi Field a reality. And, she said, the two teams are going to try to avoid that drama in the future. “We’re going to apply the lessons learned on a go-forward basis, and it’s really simple, [Johnson will] book a contingency date on any events that are scheduled for a playoff game,” Stone said. “As long as everybody’s committed to it, we won’t have that again.” Growing Pains In the WNBA, scheduling issues are nothing new, but they used to receive significantly less attention. The Dream, who were a State Farm Arena tenant until 2019, were forced to move Game 3 of the 2013 WNBA Finals, their last Finals appearance, to the 13,000-seat Gas South Arena about 25 miles away from downtown Atlanta due a conflict with Disney On Ice . Only about 5,000 fans came to that game. But in 2024, the draft class led by Caitlin Clark and current Dream player Angel Reese brought new attention to the league. WNBA games consistently started selling out NBA arenas, and teams that played in smaller venues started moving some home games to accommodate larger audiences. The Dream felt the increased demand, selling out every single home game at Gateway Center since 2024. In response, team president Morgan Shaw Parker told FOS ahead of the 2025 season that they were actively looking for ways to move into a bigger venue. Then ahead of the Finals, the team announced it had agreed to a deal with State Farm to play all of its games at the NBA venue starting next season. Brett Davis-Imagn Images Had the Dream, who quickly turned into a championship contender after trading for Reese in April , been a yearlong tenant at State Farm this season, the WNBA Finals dates likely would’ve been accounted for. State Farm CEO Steve Koonin told FOS that they plan to hold playoff dates for the Dream through the duration of their five-year deal. Many WNBA fans were clamoring for the Hawks to move regular-season games that coincided with Games 4 and 6 of the WNBA Finals. The team did adjust start times, but did not move the dates. A Sombr concert that conflicted with Game 3 in Atlanta went ahead as scheduled, and the WNBA instead changed its date. One of the reasons the WNBA could move the three games in Atlanta was because of its media partner, first-time Finals broadcaster USA Network. The network approved each rescheduling, even a less-than-ideal TV window of 12:30 p.m. ET on a Thursday. That level of flexibility is unusual in a sports media landscape constantly striving for viewership records and higher ad revenue. The NWSL, for example, worked around its seminal broadcast windows of Saturday afternoon on CBS and Sunday afternoon on ABC. Dream owner Renee Montgomery described the Finals rescheduling to FOS as a “ group project ” involving both teams, the leagues (NBA and WNBA), and broadcast partners. An NFL spokesperson told FOS the league generally gives teams playoff dates about a year and a half to two years out. An MLB spokesperson told FOS teams know about a year and a half out when the postseason will start and when the World Series will be. item.title: Lamar Jackson’s camp hits back at critics blaming him for Ravens’ struggles
item.description: Lamar Jackson ’s camp has pushed back against criticism surrounding the NFL quarterback’s injury history and availability during the Baltimore Ravens ’ disappointing season. Lamar Jackson Entertainment shared a pointed message on X Saturday, questioning whether Jackson should carry the blame for Baltimore’s problems. “So, is it Lamar’s fault again? Or are Lamar’s injuries still an unsolved mystery?” the account posted. MORE: NFL analyst rips Marlon Humphrey over controversial Baltimore remarks The message accompanied a video compilation showing the hits Jackson and other Baltimore quarterbacks have taken this season. It also highlighted poor pass protection and questioned whether the offensive line deserves greater scrutiny. So, is it Lamar’s fault again? Or are Lamar’s injuries still an unsolved mystery? 🤔🙄 pic.twitter.com/aLyV0rHlHs — Lamar Jackson Entertainment 💽 (@lamarjacksonent) November 21, 2026 The post comes after Jackson suffered a broken and dislocated right thumb against the Buffalo Bills on November 1. He sustained the injury on his first offensive snap after returning from a high ankle sprain. Jackson underwent surgery and landed on injured reserve. His recovery timeline is estimated at six to ten weeks. The quarterback had already missed three games with the ankle injury. His limited availability has fueled criticism as Baltimore struggles through a five-game losing streak. Lamar Jackson’s camp points toward wider problems in Baltimore Atlanta, Georgia, USA; Baltimore Ravens quarterback Lamar Jackson (8) during the second quarter against the Atlanta Falcons at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. Mandatory Credit: Dale Zanine-Imagn Images Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect (Reuters) The compilation also featured injuries suffered by Baltimore’s other quarterbacks. One clip showed Tyler Huntley’s turf toe, which was a season-ending injury, and another showed Jacoby Brissett taking a hard hit against the Los Angeles Chargers. The message questioned whether those injuries should also be blamed on Jackson. It effectively shifted attention toward the team’s pass protection rather than the quarterback’s durability. The video also addressed claims that Jackson falls asleep during team meetings. It included pictures showing him sitting in the front row as proof against the rumors. Jackson has appeared in only five games this season, completing 70.1% of his passes for 967 yards and six touchdowns. Baltimore has used multiple quarterbacks during his absence and now sits at 4-6. The team ranks 22nd in scoring and has struggled to maintain consistency. Jackson’s camp clearly wants critics to consider the circumstances behind his injuries. item.description: TORONTO, ONTARIO - OCTOBER 31: Kevin Gausman #34 of the Toronto Blue Jays looks on against the Los Angeles Dodgers during the first inning in game six of the 2025 World Series at Rogers Center on October 31, 2025 in Toronto, Ontario. General manager Ross Atkins and the front office are already making roster adjustments, most recently claiming shortstop Christian Cairo off waivers from the Los Angeles Dodgers and designating reliever Chase Lee for assignment. The Blue Jays are also exploring ways to strengthen their pitching staff, with free-agent possibilities such as Tarik Skubal and Freddy Peralta drawing attention as the club considers its options for 2027. But Toronto’s offseason has also brought renewed attention to a former member of its rotation whose future remains uncertain. Kevin Gausman reached free agency shortly after being traded to the Chicago Cubs. Now, as many fans remain hopeful for a reunion that would bring Gausman back, news has surfaced that he has formally closed a personal chapter in Toronto. “Gausman, who played four-and-a-half seasons with the Jays before being dealt to the Chicago Cubs at this year’s trade deadline, appears to have sold his Lawrence Park mansion after almost a month on the market,” Dan Bilicki r eported for the Toronto Sun . item.title: Arsenal loses another player to injury
item.description: Arsenal loses another player to injury Martin Zubimendi has suffered another injury just when it appeared he was about to get more opportunities to play for Arsenal. The midfielder has struggled to maintain his fitness and secure a regular place in the Gunners’ starting line-up, making the latest setback an unwanted development. Zubimendi was one of the first names on the team sheet last season, but his involvement has been reduced during the current campaign. Although Arsenal continue to regard him as an important member of the squad, he has lost his place in the starting eleven and is working to regain his position. The Spaniard impressed while representing Spain during the international break and was expected to feature against Newcastle United . However, his hopes of getting minutes in the fixture have been disrupted after suffering another fitness problem. Arteta confirms fresh injury setback Arsenal manager Mikel Arteta has confirmed that Zubimendi will miss the upcoming matches after medical examinations revealed a hamstring injury. The midfielder initially returned from international duty believing he was in good condition and was not particularly concerned about the problem. However, further assessment revealed an injury that will keep him out of action for several weeks. The development is disappointing for both the player and Arsenal, especially as he was hoping to use the coming fixtures to strengthen his claim for a regular starting position. (Photo by Justin Setterfield/Getty Images) Zubimendi faces spell on the sidelines Speaking via Arsenal Media , Arteta provided an update on the midfielder’s condition and confirmed that he would be unavailable for selection. “He’s out; unfortunately, he has a slight problem in his hamstring. “He wasn’t too concerned to be fair after the game, but after the MRI scans, it showed that there is an injury there and he’s going to be out for a few weeks.” For Arsenal, losing the Spaniard is an unwanted setback as they continue their campaign. Meanwhile, Zubimendi will be hoping to recover quickly and return in good condition so he can compete for his place in Arteta’s midfield. His immediate priority will be completing his recovery before attempting to establish himself as a regular starter again. _____________________________________________________________________________________________ ADMIN COMMENT So here are some simple rules which I must insist commenters follow…. item.title: Is there a striker you think Bayern Munich can get in January?
item.description: (Photo by Lukasz Germaniuk/Eurasia Sport Images/Getty Images) | Getty Images Bayern Munich could be heading toward an unexpectedly busy January transfer window, and the club might not have much choice but to explore the striker m arket. Harry Kane reportedly suffered a syndesmosis tear that could keep him sidelined for as long as three mont hs. Losing the England international for that length of time would be a massive blow, particularly with Bayern competing on multiple fronts and needing a reliable goal-scoring presence. Unfortunately, Kane is not the only attacking concern. Saibari is facing an extended absenc e of his own after undergoing surgery for a syndesmotic ligament injury in his right ankle, while Serge Gnabry is expected to miss the remainder of the year with a hamstring injury. That leaves Vincent Kompany with considerably fewer attacking options and puts additional pressure on the players who remain availab le. Bayern had previously been expected to avoid January business, preferring to preserve its resources for a major attacking signing next summer. However, the injury situation could force Max Eberl and Christoph Freund to reconsider that approach. A short-term loan might make the most sense. item.title: Washington Spirit provide hope and joy in a city that badly needs it
item.description: Spirit’s run to the NWSL Championship final is in part based on a positive connection with fans at a time when DC is troubled in more ways than one In the moments after the Washington Spirit’s 2-1 semi-final victory over the Utah Royals last weekend, all of Audi Field was in rapture. In the stands, around 20,000 Spirit supporters had filled the stadium to capacity, the sixth time they’d done so in 2026. They filled the place with the type of wondrous noise that’s become alien in DC sports in recent years, the type of gleeful adoration reserved for the city’s rare winners. The Spirit will return to their home stadium to face the Kansas City Current in the NWSL championship this Saturday. In short order, the Spirit’s players made their way to the north end of the stadium, taking their celebrations into the crowd with their supporters. Perhaps no player has done more to push the Spirit into not only local but national relevance than US women’s national team forward Trinity Rodman, and Rodman herself grabbed a flag from a fan, jubilantly waving it above the crowd. Moments later, she bolted back onto the field and track down the club’s owner, Michele Kang, cajoling the businesswoman into a celebratory dance. Continue reading...

item.title: Training hard and biding his time, Dele Alli has not given up on football yet
item.description: The 30-year-old former England star combines Twitch streaming with working to return to the top as a player Consider the training regime Dele Alli has followed since he left Como 18 months ago and it becomes clear why he takes exception to suggestions he has given up on football in favour of becoming an internet personality. He trains five or six days a week with Connor Peters, an elite performance coach who has worked with players including Trevoh Chalobah. They spend four days on the pitch and days in between in the gym. A typical day begins at 9am with an hour of activation and stretching before Dele heads to non-league Windsor & Eton at 11am, where he trains on the pitches and uses the facilities. Then it’s back home to use his own oxygen chamber and sauna for a recovery session. Continue reading...

item.description: Bruno Guimarães to feel the heat on Tyneside, Alex Scott’s return further cheers Cherries and Manchester City face favourite whipping boys After three Premier League defeats on the spin, Manchester City need something or someone to come along and put some pep in their step, and Fulham look like just the thing – after all, in the past 15 years these teams have played 20 times in all competitions, and City have won precisely 20 of those games. Their current run of 17 successive league wins against Fulham is the longest run of victories by one club against a single opponent in English top-flight history. It is a reflection of the changing realities of English football, and the gulf that has opened between the teams that dominate it and those who seek to challenge them, that of the top 10 such runs all but one occurred in whole or in part after 2010 and six of them have been achieved by Sheikh Mansour’s Manchester City, with Chelsea responsible for another two, Manchester United one, and Portsmouth’s postwar, 13-game supremacy over Everton – a wild ride that included two 5-0s, a 5-1, a 6-3 and a 7-0 – the anomaly. item.description: How much in player salaries did it take to earn a point in the 2026 MLS regular season? The latest batch of salaries lends some insight Lionel Messi has closer company at the top of MLS’s list of highest-paid players, thanks to another pair of former Barcelona attackers. The Inter Miami captain is still comfortably the league’s top earner, on a guaranteed compensation of $28.3m. Robert Lewandowski (Chicago Fire) and Antoine Griezmann (Orlando City) have entered the list with the second and third highest wages, while Atlanta United’s Breel Embolo, another summer signing, ranks fifth on a guaranteed compensation of $10.8m. Second-year LAFC forward Son Heung-min sits fourth on $11.2m. Casimiro, who joined Messi in Miami at the end of his contract with Manchester United, is his team’s fourth top-earner with a guaranteed compensation of $3.54m. This comes after Miami announced his signing as a non-designated player to the surprise of some as the Brazilian arrived on a Bosman transfer rather than a loan-with-purchase, as Rodrigo De Paul had last summer, to keep Miami rules compliant. The MLS Players’ Association lists Casimiro on a base salary of $896,004. Continue reading...

item.title: Danny Kelly loved football and never forgot the absurdity of earning a living talking about it | Max Rushden
item.description: The journalist and broadcaster who died last week aged 69 knew the enduring power of radio, even as the landscape changed so quickly It’s injury time at the Emirates on 29 October 2008, Arsenal are 4-3 up against Tottenham. Tom Huddlestone cushions a ball to Luka Modric, whose strike takes a deflection. It loops over Manuel Almunia and off a post into the path of Aaron Lennon, who prods it home and starts skipping towards the Spurs supporters before diving on to the ground and being enveloped by Modric, Benoît Assou-Ekotto, Darren Bent and a couple of pitch-invading fans. Pandemonium, for once, seems the apt way to describe it. But the real entertainment is happening in a radio studio at 18 Hatfields, London SE1; the old home of TalkSport. As the goal goes in, a guttural voice makes an indecipherable but very loud noise. It’s hard to transcribe – perhaps “ERRRRRAAAARRRGGHH”, or maybe “OOEEERRAAGGH”. It’s just a noise, but it’s unmistakably Danny Kelly. He regains the power of speech and follows it up with: “Gooooaaaal … Goalll Stan, Goalll at the Emirates.” Reporter Ian Abrahams and Stan Collymore join the excitement, before Danny comes back: “I LOVE FOOTBALL, STAN, I LOVE IT.” It is such a brilliant piece of radio . From one of the absolute greats. Continue reading...

item.title: Gonzalo García: ‘I love Craven Cottage – the fans can reach out and touch you’
item.description: Spain Under-21 striker admits the pace of the Premier League has surprised him but says he must stay calm over goal drought at Fulham The first thing Rita Hayworth’s great nephew says when he walks in is: “Sorry I’m late.” Gonzalo García is not late, but it’s very like him: he is impeccably polite, accommodating, and there’s an almost gentle quality to him, a calm that’s not common but can help, especially in moments when the pressure builds. There’s a reason one of the coaches standing in the rain by the pitch where Spain’s under‑21s have just finished training says everyone here loves García. The Fulham striker shakes hands, introduces himself and ducks into the dressing room to change; then a few minutes later he’s back, apologising for a wait that wasn’t one. Time to talk, so let’s start with Tinseltown, the family tale. García laughs. His great-aunt, born Margarita Carmen Cansino, was among the biggest stars in Hollywood, although he’s not sure he’s seen any of her films. His grandfather was a surgeon and others in the family followed. His uncles played rugby for Spain, but that wasn’t his thing. As for him, he enrolled in a degree in business management and analytics, and reckons he might have liked law, yet even that wasn’t his chosen field. Continue reading...

item.title: Inside women’s football’s difficult rise in Syria: ‘A joy that everyone in the country needed’
item.description: A 14-year civil war ravaged the country and ground women’s football to a halt. Today, the first glimmers of hope are beginning to emerge amid difficulty In December 2024, Syria’s under-18 women’s football team boarded a last-minute bus at midnight from Aqaba, bound for Damascus. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close. Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home. The players had been in Jordan preparing for their final match of the WAFF women’s championship, where a win against Saudi Arabia would have kept their hopes of winning the title alive. Syria pulled out amid fears that the border would close. Back home, a war that had been largely frozen for four years was suddenly moving at pace. Rebel forces had swept out of the northwest, taking Aleppo and were pushing south towards the capital, 350km away, threatening to topple the now-former president, Bashar al-Assad. Players from the provinces around Damascus made their way home. But those from Hasakah, in the country’s far north-east, spent the next three days stranded at Damascus airport, as airline staff fled and planes sat idle on the tarmac, until a bus was finally able to take them home. item.description: Seeking redemption after failing at Spurs, newly installed Crystal Palace manager has a tough challenge ahead Thomas Frank promised his wife, Nanna, he would take a year’s sabbatical after being sacked by Tottenham in February , but he couldn’t wait that long. Having received a reported £8m payoff from Spurs, he kept an extremely low profile in the first few months after an experience at the club that sources close to the 53‑year‑old have described as “traumatic”. item.title: Do good club managers necessarily make good international managers? | Jonathan Wilson
item.description: In a mailbag edition of our newsletter, we look at Mauricio Pochettino, Pep Guardiola’s international credentials and the lack of elite English managers Sign up for our free newsletter here Who should replace Mauricio Pochettino as the USMNT manager? – Tom S Although the salary I’m sure will be excellent, I think the US job is going to be a really difficult sell to a top-level coach. The 2030 World Cup is a long way away and I’m not sure the Concacaf Nations League, the Gold Cup or even the 2028 Copa América carry much appeal for a manager with European experience or aspirations. But I’m not entirely sure that sort of coach is necessarily a great idea. The last two World Cups, after all, have been won by low-key coaches who have come from within the federation and have worked with many of the players at youth level. That’s the positive from appointing from within; appointing from without is almost certainly more expensive and there’s the danger the next foreign manager does just what Mauricio Pochettino does, and has his head turned by the first vaguely attractive European job that comes calling. item.title: Familiarity of Doha drives home just how far Socceroos have come in recent years | Joey Lynch
item.description: There is increasing evidence of an evolution not only in approach but also mentality, highlighted by a return to the scene of Asian Cup heartbreak Last week’s 3-0 dismissal of Qatar at the Abdullah bin Khalifa Stadium marked the first time the Socceroos had returned to the Gulf state since their heartbreaking elimination from the Asian Cup just under three years ago. Back then, coach Graham Arnold called Doha a “home away from home” after they relocated there during the Covid pandemic, and went so far as to suggest that they would have some form of advantage at the 2022 World Cup as a result. Wandering around the city in 2026, memories rush back of Socceroos fans becoming eager participants in the takeover of the city’s souks during the World Cup. So too the feelings of sadness to see the birds still cooped up in small cages at the nearby bird market. It evokes recollections of trips on the red Metro line out to the Al Janoub Stadium in Al Wakrah, aided by the faded posters and stickers celebrating the 2022 tournament’s arrival that to this day can still be seen in shopfronts. There’s the excitement, for some, when a stray cat reminds you just how personable the local felines can be, as well as the sense of unease that remains whenever one pauses to reflect on how all this was built and the hands that did so. item.title: WSL talking points: Chelsea’s gamble pays off and have Arsenal lost fear factor?
item.description: Blues beat champions after bold substitution and Gunners’ home struggles continue with fifth consecutive WSL draw Sonia Bompastor attempted to deflect suggestions that the removal of Kadeisha Buchanan 12 minutes into Chelsea’s top-of-the-table clash with Manchester City was tactical, but few were convinced by the claim that it was down to injury. The manager said the centre-back, who had not asked to come off and walked straight down the tunnel, had taken a knock to the head in training and been assessed and cleared, but that during the game “she was not herself”. On came Veerle Buurman and the threat of Khadija Shaw was nullified, the Dutch defender restricting the golden boot favourite so well that Shaw did not manage a shot on target. Bompastor said after the game that she had not spoken to Buchanan but that she would “explain myself to her”. “I always have good relationships with the players, bring them clarity, and I’m always direct and honest so they have the information,” she said. “It won’t be any different.” Enforced or not, the substitution was a huge gamble that paid off, even after the loss of Melvine Malard to injury in the first half reduced their number of remaining in-game substitution windows to one. item.description: Plus: more speedy marathons by footballers, headed goals of the season and chairs acting as managers Mail us with all of your questions and answers “Which club team has had the most international captains playing together at one time?” asks MH Zahid. “Conversely, which international team has had the most club captains in its starting lineup at one time?” A quick web search finds a fuss being made in various corners of the internet of Chelsea’s 2009-10 squad because it contained six national team captains in Michael Ballack (Germany), Petr Cech (Czech Republic), Didier Drogba (Côte d’Ivoire), Branislav Ivanovic (Serbia), Mikel John Obi (Nigeria) and John Terry (England). These are, indeed, six people who captained their countries, playing together at one time, but crucially they were not all international captains at that time, which because we like to have our hands bound as tight as possible – no questions please – mean they are disqualified from this particular tournament. Ivanovic, you see, was not named Serbia captain until 2012 and Mikel, who was but a whippersnapper at 22 when the 2009-10 season started, was still seven years from getting his hands on the Nigeria armband. item.title: Football comes together across Spain to honour Jesús de Miguel: ‘We’ve seen how fragile life is’
item.description: Across La Liga and beyond this weekend, footballers took to the field knowing it could have been them In the final few minutes before stepping into the arena once more, heading out for his 199th Osasuna match on Saturday evening, the man who has scored more first division goals than anyone in their history stopped his teammates for a moment and told them what it meant to wear the shirt. “This is very important,” Ante Budimir began as the dressing room, their sanctuary, fell silent around him. “We don’t have this shirt today for the sake of it. He was not chosen, and nor are we. It could have happened to anyone, anyone. Let us go knowing that we’re grateful to be on the pitch: playing, watching, warming up, sitting on the bench, whatever it may be. Boys, we were not chosen: not us, not him. Let us go, gratefully. Without thought. We have a grand day before us.” With that, Osasuna’s players turned left out of the room, where they were joined in the tunnel by footballers from Athletic Club, rivals from the north, and together they went out past the little shrine of Saint Fermin on to the field. They carried white lilies and all wore the same white shirts with a No 9 on the back, a black ribbon and the name of Jesús de Miguel, the Tenerife striker who died after a collision on the pitch five days earlier at the age of 30. At almost exactly the same time, 2,000km away to the west, Tenerife’s squad were walking out at the Heliodoro Rodríguez López in Santa Cruz. They did not have anyone alongside them, wore black suits not white shirts and did not have a game to play either, not this week. Continue reading...

item.title: Next Generation 2021: why slow and steady sometimes wins the race
item.description: Our NextGen picks from five years ago show that breaking through early does not guarantee longevity or future success Read the full updates on our class of 2021 here and here In 2021, as every year, we picked 80 players from around the world who had a chance of making it in world football – 20 from the Premier League and 60 from the rest of the world – as part of our Next Generation series . We then follow these talented boys on their journeys for five years. Often it is almost impossible to predict how they will get on (OK, when Sid Lowe sent over Lamine Yamal in 2024 we had an inkling he might do well). The ball-playing central midfielder comes from a footballing family and academy staff believe his tactical awareness is born from growing up around the game. His father, Adam, played for Brighton and is now manager along the coast at Worthing FC, while Martin (his great uncle), Paul (his grandad), and Wally (his great grandad), all enjoyed careers as players. The youngest to play in the Bundesliga at 16 years and one day, youngest player to appear in the Champions League 17 days later, youngest goal scorer in Bundesliga 11 days after that and youngest player and youngest goal scorer for the Germany Under-21 team before he has turned 17.
